info.title: Gemini Decisions - Complete Parameter Reference
info.description: Use the Gemini Decisions API to have Gemini Decision 1 answer typed questions about text, images, audio, video, and PDF documents: yes/no probabilities, one option from a fixed list, or a rating on ordered levels.

post.description:
- Use `gemini-decision-1` to evaluate text, images, audio, video, and PDFs with yes/no probabilities, single-choice answers, and scores
- Returns all answers synchronously; streaming, Batch API, and context caching are not supported
- Only input tokens are billed; output is free. A minimum charge applies per request. See [Model pricing](https://evolink.ai/pricing)
- For conversation or text generation, use the [Gemini Native API](/en/api-manual/language-series/gemini/native-api/native-api-reference)

200.description: One answer per question, keyed by the question keys in the request

400.description: Invalid request. When the request content is invalid, `code` is `invalid_request` and `message` names the field and the rule that failed. Common causes: an unsupported question `type`, a `choice` or `score` question without `criteria`, fewer than 2 options or levels, an invalid question key, empty `input`, an unknown field (such as `stream`), a `mime_type` that does not match the content, or a `gs://` URI or `files/...` name. Input blocked by safety filters returns `safety`, `prohibited_content`, `blocklist`, `image_safety`, or `content_blocked`. Using this model on another endpoint returns `model_endpoint_mismatch`. HTTP error responses are not billed. Safety feedback in an HTTP 200 response is still billed; see `usage`.

model.description:
Model ID. Use `gemini-decision-1`.

This model is not a chat model and only works on this endpoint. For example, sending it to the GPT Decisions endpoint `/v1/decisions` returns `400 model_endpoint_mismatch`.

input.description: Shared input for all questions: a text string, a single content block, or an array of content blocks (text, image, audio, video, or PDF document). Input cannot be empty. Adjacent text blocks are joined in order with no separator, so add your own spaces or newlines. To pass JSON data, serialize it to a string and send it as text.

oneOf.example: I was charged twice for my order.

questions.description:
Questions to evaluate, as a map from question key to question: 1 to 1,000 questions. You choose the keys (1 to 64 characters matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`), and each answer is returned under the same key. The model never sees the keys, so write the full question in `instructions`.

| Type | Purpose | Main result |
|---|---|---|
| `noul` | Check whether a statement holds | `noul`: probability of “yes” (0.01 to 0.99) |
| `choice` | Pick one option from a fixed list | `choice`: the most likely option ID |
| `score` | Rate the input on ordered levels | `score`: probability-weighted level score |

Each question is evaluated independently against the same input and cannot see the others; question types can be mixed. If questions depend on one another, split them into separate requests. The input and all questions share a 262,144-token context window.

DecisionRequest.description: The request body accepts only `model`, `input`, and `questions`. Any other field (such as `stream`) returns `400 invalid_request`.

InputContent.description: A content block. `type` determines the other fields

data.description: Base64-encoded file bytes (inline data is limited to 100 MB per request in total). Provide either `data` or `uri`

uri.description: Public or signed HTTPS URL of the file (up to 15 MB). Google Files API URIs, `gs://` URIs, `files/...` names, and YouTube URLs are not supported. Provide either `data` or `uri`

mime_type.description: MIME type. It must match the real file format; generic types such as `application/octet-stream` are rejected

resolution.description: Optional. Media resolution, which controls token usage and visual detail

QuestionInstructions.description: The question to evaluate against `input`, written in full. Text only: a string, a text block, or an array of text blocks

criteria.description: Optional. Defines what “yes” and “no” mean when the question alone is ambiguous

Options, as a map from option ID to a description of when it applies (use an empty string `""` when the ID is self-explanatory). 2 to 255 options. Option IDs are 1 to 128 characters (up to 512 UTF-8 bytes); internal ASCII spaces are allowed, but leading or trailing spaces and control characters are not. Option IDs are sorted alphabetically (UTF-8 byte order) before evaluation, and exact ties resolve to the alphabetically first ID, so use a non-positional catch-all ID such as `other` rather than `none_of_the_above`

Level descriptions ordered from lowest to highest: 2 to 255 non-empty strings (2 to 10 recommended). Level `i` (starting at 0) is described by `criteria[i]`. Because `score` averages level indices, keep the scale linear and adjacent levels clearly distinct
example: Cosmetic: appearance only, no lost functionality.
Workaround available: a task fails, but another way works.
Fully blocked: a task fails with no workaround.

answers.description: One answer per question, keyed by the question keys in the request. Each answer’s `type` matches its question. Empty when `prompt_feedback.block_reason` is set

noul.description: Calibrated probability that the answer is “yes”, from 0.01 to 0.99; the probability of “no” is `1 - noul`. Set thresholds within this range using labeled examples from your own traffic

confidence.description: Estimated probability that the top answer is right, equal to `max(noul, 1 - noul)`

choice.description: The option ID with the highest probability

probabilities.description: Calibrated probability for each option ID, summing to 1. Probability is always spread across your options, even when none fits

confidence.description: Probability of the selected option, from 0 to 1. When it is low, consider human review or a separate yes/no scope check

score.description: Probability-weighted average of the level indices (`sum(k × probability_k)`), so it can fall between levels. Divide it by the highest level index to normalize it to 0–1

probabilities.description: Calibrated probability for each level index (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...), summing to 1. For a discrete level, take the index with the highest probability

legend.description: Description of each level index, taken from `criteria`

confidence.description: The highest probability in `probabilities`, from 0 to 1

DecisionUsage.description: Token usage. Only input tokens are billed (`total_input_tokens`): text, image, audio, video, and PDF tokens cost the same, and output is always 0. A minimum charge applies to each request. See [Model pricing](https://evolink.ai/pricing) for current prices. Context caching is not supported; repeated input is billed separately for each request. If an HTTP 200 response contains `prompt_feedback.block_reason`, input usage is still billed. If valid usage is not returned, billing uses an estimate.

total_input_tokens.description: Billable input tokens for the shared input and all questions. The shared input counts once per request regardless of how many questions you ask; each question adds only its own instructions and criteria

modality.description: Modality: `text`, `image`, or `audio`. Video frames and PDF page images are counted as `image`

total_output_tokens.description: Always 0; this model generates no text

PromptFeedback.description: Feedback from input content filters. When `block_reason` is set, the input was blocked, no questions were evaluated, and `answers` is empty. If returned with HTTP 200, the request is still billed; see `usage`.

block_reason_message.description: Details about why the input was blocked

message.description: Error description, ending with `(request id: ...)`. Provide this ID when troubleshooting
